summary: Leela Aditi Wood is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Michigan in 2005 under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers. She held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Leendert A. van Daalen (1939–1993) was an Indologist who earned an M.A. and Ph.D. from Utrecht University, studying under Jan Gonda and Henk Bodewitz. He served as Lecturer of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1966–1992) and held a post at Leiden University (1992).
Lei Huang is a Tibetologist who studied at the Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences in 2012. She was appointed Assistant Professor at Capital Normal University in 2022.

Lei Rong, a scholar of Tibetology, studied mathematics at East China Normal University (2007–2015) and completed an Erasmus Mundus Masters across the University of Oslo, University of Roehampton, and Charles University (2015–2017). She held a post at Xizang Minzu University.

Leigh Lisker (1918–2006) was a linguist and Indologist who earned a B.A. from the University of Pennsylvania (ca. 1937–1941). He subsequently served as Assistant Professor at the University of Pennsylvania from 1948 to 1989.

Lemuel Sadoc was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who received a Ph.D. from Goethe University Frankfurt by 1924. He served as Professor at St. Stephen's College, Delhi, in 1926 and taught languages at the Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad.

Leo Buschardt (1906–1966) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed an M.A. at the University of Copenhagen (1925–1935). He held library posts at the Royal Veterinary and Agricultural University (1943) and the Royal Danish Library (1944).

Leo Frobenius (1873–1938) was an archaeologist and historian. He was affiliated with the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938), and the Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte.

Leo Joachim Frachtenberg (1883–1930) was a linguist who studied at Cornell and Columbia universities, working under Franz Boas and A. V. Williams Jackson. He worked as an ethnologist at the Bureau of American Ethnology (ca. 1909–1917) and lectured at Columbia (1910–1912).

Leo M. Pruden (1937–1991) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Taitetsu Unno. He taught at Brown University (1970–1971), the Nyingma Institute (1971), and the University of Oriental Studies.

Leo Meyer (1830–1910) was a linguist and Indologist who earned a Ph.D. at Göttingen and also studied at Berlin. He held professorships at the University of Göttingen and the University of Tartu (1865–1899), and was president of the Learned Estonian Society.
Leo Rishi Nelson Jones is an Indologist attested in 2026 as studying and working as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter at the University of Hamburg.

Leo Strauss (1899–1973) was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Marburg, Freiburg, and under Ernst Cassirer. His academic appointments included positions at Cambridge, The New School, Columbia, Hamilton College, University of Chicago (ca. 1949–1969), Claremont McKenna, and St. John's College.

Leo von Mankowski (1858–1909) was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Breslau, and Vienna, where he completed his habilitation, and under Georg Bühler. He taught at Jagiellonian University as Docent of Sanskrit from 1894 and extraordinary Professor from 1904.

Leon Cyboran (1928–1977) was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Warsaw, also studying at Wroclaw and Breslau. He taught Sanskrit and Indian philosophy at Warsaw (1965–1973) and became Professor at KUL in 1973.

Leon Hurvitz (1923–1992) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Chicago and Columbia (Ph.D. ca. 1946–1959). He served as Assistant Professor at the University of Washington (ca. 1955–1971) and Professor at the University of British Columbia (1971–1988).
Leon Sommers Swartzberg Jr. (1921–2001) was an Indologist who earned an M.A. from Columbia University (1962–1966). In 1970, he held a post teaching anthropology at Southern Oregon University.

Leonard Bloomfield (1887–1949) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, and Chicago (Ph.D. 1909), and in Germany. He held faculty posts at Cincinnati, Illinois, Ohio State, Chicago, and served as Sterling Professor of Linguistics at Yale (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé (1946–) is a historian and Sinologist who studied at Leiden University from ca. 1970 to 1986. He subsequently held a faculty post at Leiden University between 1998 and 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who completed doctoral studies under Anthony Kennedy Warder and also studied under F. E. L. Priestley. He held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).
